subject: Archaeology
title: The Cardiff Giant: A Stone Man Hoax
description: One-minute skill: The Cardiff Giant: A Stone Man Hoax.

hook.text: Workers digging a well in Cardiff, New York, in 1869 unearthed a 10-foot-tall petrified man. Thousands paid to see it.

buildup.text: George Hull, a cigar maker, secretly carved the figure from gypsum and buried it to win a bet about biblical giants.

discovery.text: P.T. Barnum offered to buy it. When refused, he made his own fake and claimed Hull's was the copy.

twist.text: Scientists quickly declared it a fake — chisel marks were visible, and gypsum doesn't preserve human tissue.

climax.text: Hull confessed, but the giant kept drawing crowds. People wanted to believe. Admission fees made everyone rich.

punchline.text: The faker confessed. The public kept paying to see it anyway.

quiz.question: What happened after the Cardiff Giant was exposed as a hoax?
options: George Hull was arrested and imprisoned for fraud
People kept paying to see it anyway — wonder beat truth
The sculpture was destroyed by an angry mob
